Title: Unleashing Unprivileged eBPF Potential with Dynamic Sandboxing
Authors: Soo Yee Lim, Xueyuan Han, Thomas Pasquier
Research Gap: Static verifier bypasses can be mitigated dynamically, but context switches are slow.
Notes: Pioneered post-JIT bytecode instrumentation. Restricts heap/stack size dynamically.

Title: Hive: A Hardware-assisted Isolated Execution Environment for eBPF on AArch64
Authors: Peihua Zhang, Chenggang Wu, Xiangyu Meng, Yinqian Zhang, et al.
Keywords: ARM AArch64, PAC, MTE, CPU sandboxing
Research Gap: Addresses verifier limitations. Requires specialized AArch64 hardware instructions.
Notes: Uses unprivileged load/store instructions and pointer signatures (PAC) to avoid TLB/context switch performance costs.

Title: SafeBPF: Hardware-assisted Defense-in-depth for eBPF Kernel Extensions
Authors: Soo Yee Lim, Tanya Prasad, Xueyuan Han, Thomas Pasquier
Keywords: MTE, ARMv8.5, spatial safety, temporal safety
Research Gap: Compares software SFI with hardware-assisted MTE for deep memory tagging.
Notes: Great comparison of software vs hardware overheads.

Title: bpfbox: Simple Precise Process Confinement with eBPF
Authors: William Findlay, Anil Somayaji, David Barrera
Keywords: Linux LSM, Process Confinement, Access Control
Research Gap: Policy definitions are simple, but does not solve verifier compromise.
Notes: Early proof of using eBPF to replace heavier MAC frameworks like AppArmor.

Title: Validating the eBPF Verifier via State Embedding
Keywords: Verifier, Logic Bugs, Abstract Interpretation, Fuzzing
Research Gap: Finds logic mistakes inside verifier register range calculations automatically.
Notes: Concretized why runtime sandboxing is necessary: the verifier continues to contain critical logic bugs.

Title: eBPF-PATROL: Protective Agent for Threat Recognition and Overreach Limitation
Authors: Sangam Ghimire, Nirjal Bhurtel, Roshan Sahani, Sudan Jha
Research Gap: Combines syscall filtering with runtime context validation to stop escape attempts.
Notes: Relies on helper contexts for syscall argument validation. Useful reference for runtime architectures.

Title: eBPF Security Threat Model
Authors: Jack Kelly, James Callaghan, Andrew Martin
Keywords: eBPF Threat Model, Attack Trees, CAP_BPF, Security Controls
Research Gap: Comprehensive breakdown of attack vectors; lacks technical implementation scripts.
Notes: Establishes standardized terminology for threats (confidentiality, integrity, evasion, DOS).
